item.title: Advancements in intraoperative monitoring techniques in neurosurgical practice: a systematic review
item.description: Abstract Background Intraoperative monitoring (IOM) has become a vital component of contemporary neurosurgery, significantly reducing neurological deficits and improving surgical outcomes. This systematic review aims to evaluate recent advancements in IOM techniques in neurosurgical practice.

item.title: Constant-round quantum advantage in communication complexity for total functions
item.description: We show that there exists a total function for which there is a polynomial gap between the randomized and the constant-round quantum communication complexity. Previously, such a separation was known only for quantum protocols using polynomially many rounds.

item.title: Development of a Deep Learning Model for Real-Time Monitoring of Anesthesia Depth and Its Clinical Validation
item.description: Real-time anesthesia depth monitoring is essential to mitigate awareness and over-hypnosis risks, yet most indices are prone to artifact sensitivity and inter-patient variation. This study developed a causal deep learning pipeline for streaming physiological windows, including a temporal convolutional neural network encoder, temporal dependency module, attention-based aggregation, and an optional uncertainty head.

item.title: Variational Quantum Circuit Parameterization of SchNet: A Simulator-Based Feasibility Study for Conservative Molecular Force Fields
item.description: Machine-learning force fields provide a promising route for accelerating molecular simulation by replacing expensive quantum-chemical calculations with differentiable models of molecular energies and atomic forces. However, learning accurate and energy-conserving forces remains challenging, especially when the model must capture both global energy trends and local potential-energy gradients from limited data.

item.title: Physics-Based versus Data-Driven Classification of Single-Photon Quantum Emitters from Sparse Autocorrelation Data
item.description: Identifying single photon emitters from large, inhomogeneous candidate populations is key to realizing many quantum applications. This requires measuring the emitters second order autocorrelation function, whose statistical reliability is fundamentally limited by acquisition time.

item.title: Quantum Mechanics as Partial Closure: Deriving Information, Decoherence, Measurement, and the Emergence of Local Classicality
item.description: Quantum mechanics represents physical states through complex amplitudes, state vectors, and density operators, yet the ontological status of these objects remains interpretation-dependent. This paper develops a closure-based formulation in which a quantum state is interpreted as a representation of contextually partial relational closure: the state possesses definite mathematical and relational structure while remaining unresolved relative to one or more observational contexts.

item.title: Quantum algorithm for differential equations via permutation matrix representation with application to the Burgers equation
item.description: We develop a quantum algorithm for solving the dynamics of the nonlinear viscous Burgers equation. We apply the Carleman linearization procedure on the spatially discretized equation, followed by a padding scheme that allows implementation on qubit registers.
